name: Steve Bannon

summary.text: Stephen K. Bannon is a media executive and political strategist who served as vice president and secretary of Cambridge Analytica from June 2014 to August 2016 according to his publicly filed financial disclosure, then as chief executive of Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and as White House chief strategist. In 2018 whistleblower Christopher Wylie told House Democrats that Bannon directed Cambridge Analytica staff to test messaging about Vladimir Putin in 2014, and the Senate Intelligence Committee examined his role with the firm. Trump pardoned Bannon in January 2021 in the federal 'We Build the Wall' case; on February 11, 2025 he pleaded guilty in New York state court to one count of scheme to defraud in the first degree and received a three-year conditional discharge.

facts.claim: Bannon served as vice president and secretary of Cambridge Analytica from June 2014 to August 2016, when he became chief executive of Trump's presidential campaign, according to his publicly filed financial disclosure as reported by The Washington Post.
facts.quote: He served as vice president and secretary of Cambridge Analytica from June 2014 to August 2016, when he became chief executive of Trump's campaign, according to his publicly filed financial disclosure.

facts.claim: In an April 2018 interview with House Judiciary and Oversight Committee Democrats, former Cambridge Analytica employee Christopher Wylie said Bannon directed staff in 2014 to test messaging about Russian president Vladimir Putin and Russian expansion in Eastern Europe, and that Bannon was involved in 2013 in discussing possible projects before formally becoming vice president in 2014.
facts.quote: Steve Bannon directed staff to test messaging in 2014 about Russian president Vladmir Putin and Russian expansion in Eastern Europe

sources.publisher: House Committee on Oversight and Reform Democrats

facts.claim: In 2018 Reuters reported that the U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee was pursuing a wide-ranging investigation into Bannon's activities during the 2016 campaign, including his role with Cambridge Analytica, and was arranging a staff interview; Bannon's lawyer said the committee had expressed interest in interviewing him as a witness.
facts.quote: the panel also will examine Bannon's role with Cambridge Analytica

sources.title: Steve Bannon faces U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee probe over 2016 campaign
Sources: US Senate Panel Probes Former Trump Aide Bannon

facts.claim: On February 11, 2025 Bannon pleaded guilty in New York state court to one count of scheme to defraud in the first degree in the 'We Build the Wall' case brought by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg; five other charges were dropped, Judge April Newbauer imposed a three-year conditional discharge with no prison time, and Bannon was barred from fundraising for or serving as an officer, director or fiduciary of any charity with assets in New York.
facts.quote: In exchange for pleading guilty to one count of scheming to defraud in the first degree, he received a sentence of conditional discharge for three years.

facts.claim: Trump pardoned Bannon in January 2021 in connection with federal charges related to the 'We Build the Wall' organization; the 2025 New York state case was separate from that federal matter. Bannon has called the state case a political persecution.

openQuestions: Bannon's own financial disclosure form (OGE 278e) was not opened; the June 2014 to August 2016 dates rest on The Washington Post's account of it.
Whether the Senate Intelligence Committee ultimately interviewed Bannon and what its final report said about Cambridge Analytica was not researched.
The House Oversight release of Epstein-estate calendars naming Bannon is recorded in the elon-musk and valar-ventures files and was not duplicated here.
Wylie's statements to House Democrats are recorded as 'words' because they are testimony, not findings.

The brief's statement that Bannon described himself as Cambridge Analytica's vice-president in House testimony was not confirmed; in the House Intelligence interview he described helping put the company together. The vice-president title rests on his OGE financial disclosure as reported by The Washington Post (already recorded).
The full House Intelligence Committee transcript (sb2a.pdf) was not read; the quoted lines come from Business Insider's account.
